My name is Lana Abed, and I am a third-year Textile Design student. I am passionate about textiles, colors, patterns, and creative design. Through my studies, I explore different materials and techniques to create unique and meaningful textile designs.

I enjoy learning new skills, developing creative ideas, and experimenting with fabrics and textures. My goal is to continue growing as a designer and create work that combines aesthetics, innovation, and personal expression.

The Inspiration

"Nature as
the first
textile"

The starting point for this collection was the pink oyster mushroom — a living organism whose layered, folded caps, delicate gills, and soft terracotta tones became the blueprint for textile exploration. The mushroom's natural structure mirrors what fabric can do: layer, drape, fray, and fold.

Working on the knitting machine, each sample was developed to echo the organic logic of the mushroom — ribbed textures like gill patterns, fringe that mimics spore-releasing edges, and a color palette pulled directly from the coral flesh of the fungus itself. Nature became the first sketch.

01

Selected Work

Project 01 — Knitwear

Organic Layers

A sculptural knitwear cape directly inspired by the layered caps and gill structure of the pink oyster mushroom. The garment combines two distinct knit techniques — a ribbed base layer and a textured outer layer — joined at the edges with tiny gold ring hardware that echoes the mushroom's delicate fringe.

The terracotta and coral palette was derived directly from the mushroom itself. The cape can be draped in multiple ways, making it a wearable piece of organic sculpture.

Machine Knit Nature-Inspired Sculptural Multi-wear
Project 02 — Mixed Media

Red Organic Form

A bold wearable textile work constructed from open-weave red fabric layered with hand-embroidered sequin patches in deep purple and burgundy. The flowing, asymmetric form wraps dramatically around the body, exploring the boundary between garment and art object.

The piece celebrates raw edges and movement — the expressive potential of textile as sculpture. The contrast of airy mesh against dense embroidery creates a rich visual dialogue between lightness and depth.

Open Weave Embroidery Sequin Work Wearable Art
Project 03 — Sportswear

Botanical Activewear

An activewear project exploring the contrast between delicate botanical print and performance-oriented silhouettes. A lightweight floral jacket — translucent and garden-inspired — is layered over a seamless ribbed blue set.

The project examines how print design can transform function-first sportswear into expressive fashion, bridging performance aesthetics and personal style.

✦ Created using Digital Textile Design

Print Design Activewear Botanical Seamless Knit
Project 04 — Woven Textile Design / עיצוב אריג

Orange Woven Scarf

A hand-woven textile piece created on a loom — a woven fabric design that explores color, rhythm, and structure through the interlacing of threads. The vivid orange striped scarf, with its raw fringe edges, is styled as a wearable accessory that bridges traditional craft and contemporary fashion.

Children's Collection

Project 04

Children's Textile

A children's clothing project exploring playful yet refined design. The collection focuses on natural fabrics, gentle silhouettes, and thoughtful proportions — creating garments that allow freedom of movement while maintaining a clean, warm aesthetic. The editorial styling emphasizes natural light and everyday tenderness.
